_what: ADR-017 enforcement ledger (WEBVIEW ONLY). Same contract as ADR-015's: an entry is a KNOWN pre-ruling violation with its reason; the test fails on an unlisted violation, on a listed entry that no longer violates, and on an entry without a reason. Moved here 2026-08-29 (PL-17) from the ADR-015 ledger, where a pure React rule had been enforced under a document that mentions React zero times. `bundleStylesheets` rows are ADR-017 §6 violations found by webview-stylesheet-bundles.test.ts. `dynamicClassSiteCeiling` is a RATCHET, not an exemption: it counts className expressions this check cannot read statically (template literals), so it measures how much of the surface is NOT covered. It may only go down.

_dynamicClassSiteCeiling_note: 151 -> 123 on 2026-08-29 by converting 10 template-literal className expressions to cn(), which this check can read. IMPORTANT: this number counts SITES PER BUNDLE, not distinct files — a shared component in five bundles contributes five. The distinct-site count is far smaller (36 before the conversion, of which 23 were `className={someProp}` pass-throughs whose real class is checked at the CALL site, so never a blind spot). What remains is one genuinely dynamic case (InlineNotice builds `inline-notice--${tone}`) and two helper-call sites, multiplied across bundles. 123 -> 105 on 2026-08-31 by PL-31: with the UI barrels gone, a bundle imports only the components it uses instead of everything the barrel re-exported, so the same dynamic-className sites are multiplied across fewer bundles. The count is sites PER BUNDLE, which is why deleting no component at all moved it. Then 105 -> 95 as the remaining UI barrels went (same cause).

_classesDefinedNowhere_note: Classes a component asks for that NO stylesheet in that bundle defines — and that no stylesheet anywhere in src/ defines either. A different defect from bundleStylesheets, with a different fix: for these, either the rule was never written or the markup is dead. Seeded at 21 on 2026-08-29 so the set cannot GROW while it is triaged; the triage itself is PL-20. Two are visible bugs already (.text-red-500 on an error icon, .text-orange-700 on warning text) — they render with no colour. Note .text-red-500 IS defined, but inside VerifiedField's inline <style> block, so it exists only where that component is mounted; the scanner counts style-block classes as defined within their own bundle, which is why this reports only the bundles VerifiedField does not reach.

_styleBlockLeaks_note: Thirteen classes defined in a component <style> block AND used by another component. NONE is broken: every one is also defined in custom-spectrum.css, which all eight bundle entries import — so these are redundant copies shadowing a global sheet, not missing styles. Deleting them is not free: the global copies carry !important in places and the inline ones do not, so removal can change which declaration wins. That needs webview-visual-baseline and belongs to PL-21. This ledger stops the set growing meanwhile.
_inlineStyleCeilings_note: Pinned 2026-08-30. The per-file cap of five static inline styles in inline-styles.test.ts bounds any ONE file and says nothing about the total; these pin the aggregate so the direction of travel is one way. Static and dynamic are pinned separately so removing a static one cannot be paid for by adding a dynamic one.
_godFileTopLevelRules_note: Top-level rules in custom-spectrum.css. The CONTROL for featureRulesInGlobalSheet: if that falls while this does not, rules were relabelled rather than moved out. Measured 920 on 2026-09-08 at the start of the CSS migration (.rptc/plans/css-architecture-migration). Target is the utility count, ~235 — at which point the file is a utility sheet, not a god file. NOTE ON COMPARABILITY: the parser gained element-led brace lines on 2026-09-09, which makes one previously invisible rule countable. A pin set before that date is one lower than the same file measured today. 95 -> 77 on 2026-09-09: .inline-notice-*, .inline-rename-* and .inline-action-link (18 rules) to src/core/ui/styles/inline-controls.css. `--check` REFUSED this one — the two counts fell by 18 and 0 — and it was right to: those 18 had been counted as UTILITIES because the prefix rule reads `inline`, which the utility list names. Two shared components were sitting in the utility sheet looking like part of the spacing scale, which is why that file still read as disorganised after step 2 was called done. The divergence is the finding, not an error.

_vendorLayerBundles_note: A FLOOR, not a ceiling — it counts up. How many of the eight webview bundles ship vendor CSS in a cascade layer below ours (ADR-018 §1). 0 of 8 on 2026-09-08. This is also PL-33's one unenforced convention: 'vendor CSS sits in the lowest cascade layer' cannot be enforced while it is true of zero bundles, and becomes enforceable at 8. Gated on step 2 — until custom-spectrum is split, all eight entries import it and there is no seam to flip one surface through.
_capturedProperties_note: A FLOOR. How many CSS properties the visual fingerprint records (.claude/skills/webview-visual-baseline/capture.js PROPS). The net may get sharper and may never get blunter: a migration verified by a coarsening net is unverified and looks identical to a verified one. 16 originally; 23 after the ADR-018 self-audit; 26 on 2026-09-08 when deleting a letter-spacing rule produced an empty diff that proved nothing.
_interactionCells_note: A FLOOR. Cells captured by capture-interactions.js — 42 interactive elements across 8 surfaces at rest/hover/focus/active. Measured 2026-09-08. Known gap kept deliberately visible: the sidebar's 6 interactive elements respond to NO forced pseudo-state, so its interaction styling is invisible to this instrument and a clean sidebar row is not evidence.
_stylesheetOwner_note: ADR-017 §7: a non-base sheet under src/core/ui/styles/ may only define classes a component under src/core/ui/components/ actually uses. EMPTY on purpose — the one violation its first run found (.integrations-*, the integrations surface's shell and grid, batched into shared-ui.css) was fixed rather than ledgered, by moving it to src/features/dashboard/ui/styles/integrations.css. A row here would be a sheet we have decided to leave in the wrong place, and there is no such sheet today.
_unlayeredRuleCeiling_note: Rules outside EVERY cascade layer. Unlayered beats layered for a normal declaration, so a loose rule silently outranks everything in `theme` — and 135 of them is why a rule that looks like it should win sometimes does not. A RATCHET, not a ban: emptying it moves pixels and belongs to the cascade flip (ADR-018 step 3), not to a convention. Measured 2026-09-09 across nine sheets; the biggest are data-installer.css (49), connect-services.css (26) and index.css (19). 135 -> 0 the same day. The prediction was that layering them would DEMOTE them below Spectrum's unlayered CSS and break 128 plain rules; measured, it moved NOTHING — empty resting diff across 2,700 elements and empty interaction diff across 168 cells. Being unlayered only matters where a vendor rule actually competes for the same property on the same element, and for these it does not. A ban now rather than a ratchet: the number is 0 and a new loose rule is a build failure.
